pace.source: convention (matches the scene duration floor/ceiling) — not yet tuned to the director's actual preference
pace.note: seconds per stimulus/event. This is the director's pacing taste, not a physical constant — refine it the same way as speed: when a gap gets filled with a known count of media at a known total duration, that's a data point. No calibration command for it yet; adjust by hand in the meantime.

calibration.source: Drone Part 1 — 5 sections, 486 words, script reconstructed from takes 1/3/4/5/6
calibration.caveat: measured take lengths include leading/trailing silence and pre-retake stutters, so real speech is slightly faster than 3.11 w/s. An earlier, uncalibrated ~2.4 w/s estimate does not reproduce against these takes at the section level — treat 3.1 w/s as the working voiceover rate until a cleaner measurement contradicts it.
calibration.text_rates_uncalibrated: text_lead / text_per_word / text_min are conventions, not measurements. Nothing has been recorded to fit them.

notes: refit with `estimate.py calibrate clock.json measured.json --write` after every new recording; the fit lands in `speed`, so rebase it into w0/ks/pauses when it settles
